title: Checkpoint: Climate Change
objective: After this level you can explain what the evidence shows about recent warming, what causes it and what it is changing.
summary: The chain of evidence: rising CO2, fossil fingerprints, about 1.1 °C of measured warming, natural causes ruled out and feedbacks amplifying. The IPCC calls human influence unequivocal.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 finale: build the case for a warming world, one link at a time.
cards.body: A strong case needs evidence that the change is real, that it's ours and that it matters. You have gathered all three. Now chain them together.

cards.headline: The chain of evidence
cards.body: Link one: carbon dioxide has climbed every year since the record began in 1958. Link two: its carbon-13 and carbon-14 fingerprints point to fossil fuels. Link three: thermometers on land and sea show about 1.1 °C of warming. Link four: the Sun and volcanoes add almost nothing. Link five: feedbacks amplify the push. Pull on any link and it holds, because each one rests on separate measurements.

cards.fact: The IPCC calls it unequivocal: human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land.
cards.context: The same report says the rise in greenhouse gases since around 1750 is unequivocally caused by human activities. Where the science is still open, such as tornadoes or how fast the ice sheets will go, it says that just as plainly.

mascot.line: This is the whole chapter in one sentence. Levels 81 to 89 are the reasons behind it.

cards.headline: Chapter 9 complete
learned: How scientists know recent warming is mainly caused by human greenhouse gases, not the Sun or volcanoes.
Why the Keeling Curve climbs every year and zigzags with the seasons.
How feedbacks from snow and water vapor amplify warming, and why sensitivity is still a range.
What warming is already changing, from shrinking ice sheets to hotter heatwaves and heavier rain.

questions.prompt: Climate Change recap: which word does the IPCC use for human influence having warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land?

options.label: Possible
options.rationale: The IPCC uses a much stronger word.

options.label: Unequivocal
Unproven
Temporary
options.rationale: That describes volcanic cooling, not this finding.

questions.explanation: The IPCC calls it unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land.

questions.prompt: Climate Change recap: which pair of clues shows the extra carbon dioxide comes from burning fossil fuels?

options.label: The Keeling Curve's yearly zigzag and May peak
options.rationale: That zigzag is plants growing and decaying.

options.label: Falling carbon-13 and falling oxygen in the air
A cooling stratosphere and a steady Sun
options.rationale: Those clues clear the Sun, not identify the carbon.

options.label: Hotter heatwaves and heavier downpours
options.rationale: Those are effects of warming, not its source.

questions.explanation: Fossil carbon is low in carbon-13, and burning it uses up oxygen: both clues point to fossil fuels.

questions.prompt: Climate Change recap: why does the Keeling Curve rise a little higher every year?

options.label: Plants release more CO2 each spring
options.rationale: Spring growth pulls CO2 out of the air.

options.label: Volcanoes are erupting more often
options.rationale: Humans emit far more CO2 than volcanoes.

options.label: Sinks absorb only about half our emissions
The Mauna Loa volcano leaks CO2 into the samples
options.rationale: The record rises the same way worldwide.

questions.explanation: Plants and the ocean take up about half of the CO2 we emit; the rest accumulates in the air.

questions.prompt: Climate Change recap: why is water vapor called a feedback rather than the cause of warming?

options.label: It follows temperature, raining out in about nine days
It is not a greenhouse gas at all
options.rationale: It is Earth's most abundant greenhouse gas.

options.label: It stays in the air for thousands of years
options.rationale: A vapor molecule lasts only about nine days.

options.label: It cools the planet by blocking the Sun
options.rationale: Vapor traps heat and amplifies warming.

questions.explanation: Vapor rains out within days, so its amount follows temperature; it amplifies warming started by other gases.

questions.prompt: Climate Change recap: a big eruption, like the one in Level 1, cools Earth for a year or two. How does that appear in the long temperature record?

options.label: It reverses the warming trend for good
options.rationale: Eruption cooling fades within one to three years.

options.label: As a brief dip on top of the upward trend
As a permanent step down in temperature
It is invisible, since volcanoes can't cool Earth
options.rationale: Big eruptions do cool the planet briefly.

questions.explanation: Eruption cooling lasts one to three years, so it shows as a short dip while the long rise continues.
